method: Focused adversarial search, not systematic-review completeness or formal GRADE/AMSTAR scoring

sources.citation: Held S et al. Maximizing Adaptations in Concurrent Training: An Umbrella Review of Meta-analyses. Sports Med. 2026;56:1489-1512.
sources.design: Umbrella review; 17 meta-analyses; publisher reports 144 studies, 1492 healthy participants; search through 2025-02-28
sources.quality_appraisal: High-level synthesis but detailed risk-of-bias/overlap extraction unavailable; no independent quality rating inferred from label
sources.finding: Aggregated CT adaptations compatible with broad fitness aims; highly trained/elite data scarce. No general sequencing difference established in the abstract.
sources.applicability: Background compatibility in recreational healthy adults, not acute recovery or exact S01/S02 schedule
sources.limitations: Abstract wording contains a nonsignificance/trend inconsistency in sequence reporting; no exact effect, sequencing rule or prescription is derived. Umbrella overlap prevents counting reviews as independent replication.
sources.notice_check: No correction/retraction notice observed on retrieved publisher record; targeted identifier searches; not exhaustive

sources.citation: Schumann M et al. Compatibility of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training for Skeletal Muscle Size and Function: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Sports Med. 2022;52:601-612 (online 2021).
sources.design: 43 studies; healthy adults, supervised CT >=4 weeks versus identical strength prescription without aerobic training
sources.quality_appraisal: Systematic random-effects synthesis; heterogeneous interventions and subgroup precision limit generalization; no fresh formal scoring
sources.finding: Pooled maximal strength and hypertrophy differences were not significant; explosive strength attenuation was detected, more pronounced same-session. Lack of significance does not establish equivalence or zero individual risk.
sources.applicability: Chronic endpoint-specific compatibility; protects against universal no-interference claim
sources.limitations: Not a study of next-morning threshold after this lower. Its >=3-hour subgroup cannot become a universal recovery cutoff. Acute readiness and elite optimization not proven.
sources.notice_check: No notice observed on accessed record; targeted title correction/retraction query; not exhaustive

sources.citation: Huiberts RO, Wust RCI, van der Zwaard S. Concurrent Strength and Endurance Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis on the Impact of Sex and Training Status. Sports Med. 2024;54:485-503 (online 2023).
sources.design: 59 studies; 1346 healthy adults aged 18-50; >=4 weeks; strength, power, hypertrophy and VO2max
sources.quality_appraisal: Cochrane bias assessment reported; many unclear risks; female/highly trained underrepresentation; variable design/status definitions
sources.finding: Lower-strength adaptations attenuated in male subgroup, not clearly in female subgroup; untrained endurance subgroup had attenuated VO2max gains. Does not predict any individual's response.
sources.applicability: Counterevidence to universal compatibility and one-dimensional training-level labels
sources.limitations: Different pooled populations/comparators from SS2; subgroup results do not show sex alone causes interference. Sparse female/highly trained data and only about 60% complete dual-status descriptors; overlap with other reviews.
sources.notice_check: No correction/retraction notice observed on retrieved publisher record; not exhaustive

sources.citation: Currier BS et al. American College of Sports Medicine Position Stand. Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2026;58:851-872.
sources.design: Position stand/overview; 137 systematic reviews, >30000 participants, healthy adults >=18, RT >=6 weeks; search current October2024
sources.quality_appraisal: Recognized evidence-based position stand; individual recommendations not independently extracted/graded here
sources.finding: Updates 2009 stand. Progressive RT improves multiple outcomes; prescription should reflect the intended outcome. Equipment type did not consistently determine outcomes.
sources.applicability: Adult general-strength candidate scope; supports investigating compatible home/equipment routes, not equivalence of particular exercises
sources.limitations: No exact sets/load/frequency threshold is adopted. General healthy-adult findings do not approve this catalog, eligibility, advanced performance or simultaneous-program dose.
sources.notice_check: No notice observed in accessible indexed record; targeted title correction/retraction query; not exhaustive

sources.citation: de Carvalho e Silva GI et al. Acute Neuromuscular, Physiological and Performance Responses After Strength Training in Runners: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Sports Med Open. 2022;8:105.
sources.design: 19 studies qualitative/13 quantitative; male recreational/trained runners; acute strength protocols; literature through April2021
sources.quality_appraisal: Included protocols heterogeneous, including deliberately damaging and potentiation protocols; authors judged quality fair; performance not meta-analyzed. Some reported standardized effect magnitudes/units warrant caution; no magnitude used.
sources.finding: Some neuromuscular/soreness/perceived-exertion outcomes deteriorated, whereas several submaximal physiological measures did not. Direct performance responses varied; exact time course was not robustly resolved.
sources.applicability: Acute interference is a plausible question, independently of chronic CT compatibility
sources.limitations: Male-only evidence, disparate protocols and timepoints; neither 12h unsafe nor 24/36h sufficient is established. Abstract's broad TTE wording is narrowed by full text reporting one non-significant TTE study.
sources.notice_check: No notice observed on PubMed/publisher record; targeted identifier correction/retraction query; not exhaustive

sources.citation: Campos Y et al. Training-intensity Distribution on Middle- and Long-distance Runners: A Systematic Review. Int J Sports Med. 2022;43:305-316.
sources.design: Systematic review, 20 articles on running intensity distribution and quantification
sources.quality_appraisal: No full-text bias assessment read; measurement-method differences explicit in abstract
sources.finding: Different intensity-quantification methods can classify the same program differently.
sources.applicability: Measurement caution; no universal intensity distribution adopted
sources.limitations: Cannot validate RPE6 as threshold or turn reported 70/30 split into a universal hybrid prescription.

sources.citation: Nuuttila OP et al. The accuracy of fixed intensity anchors to estimate lactate thresholds in recreational runners. Eur J Appl Physiol. 2025;125:2161-2171.
sources.design: Original threshold measurement study; 165 recreational runners, 64 female/101 male; incremental treadmill tests
sources.quality_appraisal: Direct measurement-method question, not randomized program effectiveness; single sample/test method
sources.finding: Fixed-anchor estimates had individual error; RPE-derived thresholds were least accurate among compared estimates in this sample.
sources.applicability: Direct counterexample to RPE6 guaranteeing a physiological threshold
sources.limitations: Does not invalidate RPE for training or require lab testing for all; no universal alternative anchor or dose follows. Threshold method/sample/context matter. Methods used Finnish-translated Borg6-20; fixture uses unanchored0-10. No numeric/scale transfer or direct test of fixture RPE6/10 is justified.

sources.citation: Cowley N et al. Effects of different resistance training loads, exercises, and volume-regulated proximities to failure on acute and short-term neuromuscular, perceptual, and metabolic responses. J Sports Sci. 2026;44:1877-1896.
sources.design: Randomized crossover; 18 participants, six-set squat/prone-row sessions, 65/85%1RM and failure/1RIR/3RIR; 24h followup
sources.quality_appraisal: Small acute controlled study, volume/repetitions differ across proximity conditions; full methods not assessed
sources.finding: Fatigue responses differed with load, exercise and proximity to failure in this protocol.
sources.applicability: Auxiliary evidence against identity-only fatigue inference
sources.limitations: Not this squat/RDL/split combination, not 12h threshold; no extrapolation to numerical fatigue savings or minimum effective dose.

sources.citation: Riebe D et al. Updating ACSM's Recommendations for Exercise Preparticipation Health Screening. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2015;47:2473-2479.
sources.quality_appraisal: Consensus contextual boundary; not complete current screening algorithm validation
sources.finding: Screening considers activity, symptoms/known disease and intended intensity; unnecessary blanket medical referrals can create barriers.
sources.applicability: Supports separating missing information from confirmed clinical concern, without implementing clinical screening
sources.limitations: No diagnosis, contraindication rule or clearance generated; specialty/current clinical guidance and human professionals remain necessary for clinical issues. User/constitution establishes the agent's boundary, not this paper.
